2011_030_120611regmtg.paragraph: The Troy School District Board of Education packet for the regular meeting of Tuesday, December 6, 2011, 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, pairs the October 2011 Treasurer's Report and a full October check register with reports on full-day kindergarten, the Summer Success Academy, and the Facilities Study, plus MESSA and policyholder resolutions. The check register totals $3,318,441.42 across all funds, and total disbursements in the period are reported as $6,307,840.15. The Business item asks the Board to certify compliance with at least four of five criteria under Section 22f of the State School Aid Act to claim the $100 per pupil Best Practices incentive.

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting, Tuesday, December 6, 2011, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW).

**Recognition**
Troy High physics teacher John Morrison and physics club students won Lemelson-MIT InvenTeam status for a mechanical-assist stair climber, one of 15 high school teams nationally, with a $10,000 prototype award and a June showcase at EurekaFest on the MIT campus in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

**Consent agenda**
November 1, 2011 minutes; November 15, 2011 workshop minutes; October 2011 Treasurer's Report. The November 1 meeting (7:00 p.m.–8:48 p.m., President Philippart presiding) passed Resolution 11-098 (consent), 11-099 (new hire Melissa Marsack) and 11-100 accepting the audited 2011 financial statements presented by Plante & Moran's Teresa Pollock with an unqualified opinion — each 7 ayes, 0 nays. Recognitions included Heather Kelly (ArtPrize 2011, "Wish Project"), Rebecca Brewer (2011 ING Unsung Heroes, $27,000 for "Mini-Med School – Simulating Surgeries"), the HealthierUS School Challenge Bronze Award (banner, plaque and $500 to each of 12 elementary schools), and Robert Stromayer's 23 years at Niles Continuing Education.

**Identification.** Board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting held Tuesday, December 6, 2011 at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; the district masthead gives 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except July and August. Agenda page references: Recognition p. 4; Consent Agenda p. 5; November 1 minutes p. 6; November 15 workshop minutes p. 16; Treasurer's Report p. 17; MESSA Agreement p. 87; Policyholder Resolution p. 92; Full-Day Kindergarten p. 93; Summer Success Academy Follow-Up p. 111; Best Practices Resolution p. 123; Facilities Study Update p. 125; NSBA conference p. 133; Closed Session p. 134.

**Recognition.** Troy High School physics teacher John Morrison and physics club students Sandeep Arakali, David Bai, Nitin Chandra, Allen Chen, Kathy Chen, Matthew Cui, Rolland He, Lawrence Kim, Maxwell Li, Richard Mu, Nikhil Ramu, Phillip Yang, Clark Zhang and Arnold Zhou won Lemelson-MIT InvenTeam status for an innovative mechanical-assist stair climber, one of 15 high school teams nationally, receiving $10,000 to develop a prototype and showcasing at EurekaFest on the MIT campus, Cambridge, Massachusetts, in June.

**Minutes of November 1, 2011.** Called to order 7:00 p.m. by President Philippart, adjourned 8:48 p.m.; Board members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Malven, Miletti and Underwood present with two student representatives, Superintendent Fowler and administrators Birmingham, Colligan, Keeling, Machesky, Mull, Papasian, Rajter and Witt, plus about 20 audience members. Heather Kelly's mixed-media "Wish Project" was shown at ArtPrize 2011 in Grand Rapids. AP biology teacher Rebecca Brewer was named the nation's most innovative educator in the 2011 ING Unsung Heroes Awards Program and received $27,000 for "Mini-Med School – Simulating Surgeries," moving 11th and 12th grade biology students from dissection to mock surgical procedures. The district earned the HealthierUS School Challenge Bronze Award, with each school receiving a banner, plaque and $500; Sodexo General Manager Gayle Moran reported the invitation to join First Lady Michelle Obama at the White House, and 12 elementary schools were recognized: Barnard, Bemis, Costello, Hamilton, Hill, Leonard, Martell, Morse, Schroeder, Troy Union, Wass and Wattles. Robert Stromayer, Director of Niles Continuing Education, was recognized for 23 years of service. Resolution 11-098 approved the October 4 minutes, October 18 workshop minutes, September 2011 Treasurer's Report and a spring athletic supplies bid award (7-0); Resolution 11-099 approved new hire Melissa Marsack (7-0); Resolution 11-100 accepted the audited 2011 financial statements presented by Plante & Moran auditor Teresa Pollock, who issued an unqualified opinion after a draft was reviewed at the October 18, 2011 workshop, with thanks to Mark Rajter and Monica Papasian (7-0). Ron Keoleian and Merri Lynn Colligan reported on iPads purchased with 2004 technology bond monies as part of the laptop refresh, distributed 30 devices per building in two carts of 15; Mrs. Fleming wished the district had more than 660 iPads, and Mr. Keoleian noted laptops take approximately three to four minutes to power up and log in. Anne Mull reported rising MEAP and MME cut scores — old standards required 39% of answers correct, new standards 65% — with Smarter Balanced computer adaptive assessments of the Common Core State Standards first administered in 2015, the MEAP minimally modified in 2012, the last MEAP given in the fall of 2013, artificial-intelligence scoring, and a State Board decision to continue social studies and science MEAP testing beyond 2014. The Facilities Study Team of 18 community members, co-chaired by Greg Bryen and Waqar Hashim and managed by Stu Redpath and Mike Zinn, met October 28 and 29 and will present findings at the February 7, 2012 meeting. Dr. Fowler reviewed five 2011/2012 superintendent goals. Student representatives Maggie Steele (Troy High, fall play "Almost Maine") and Jonny Dowdall (Athens: first back-to-back winning seasons since 1994, OAA Red Division Football Coach of the Year Josh Heppner, varsity tennis All-Academic Team Award with a 3.93 cumulative GPA, National Merit reception November 9, Jennifer Wang 17th in the State Golf Finals, Marching Band at State competition November 5 ranked 7th in the State) reported. Mrs. Fleming noted Tuesday, November 8 as Voting Day with three seats open on the Troy School Board. Minutes submitted by Paula Fleming, Secretary.

**Minutes of November 15, 2011 workshop.** Administration Building, 6:00 p.m. to 9:13 p.m.; all seven members present with Dr. Fowler, Mrs. Jagels, Mrs. Keeling, Dr. Machesky, Ms. Dixon, Mr. Hahn, Mrs. Acord and Mr. Pass and about eight other attendees. **Personnel resolutions.** Item 6.A authorizes execution of the MESSA Employer Participation Agreement for Group Welfare Benefit Programs, citing Section 22f(1) of the State School Aid Act, 2011 PA 62, which pays incentives to districts meeting at least four of five best practices including being the policyholder for medical, pharmacy, dental, vision, disability, long-term care and other healthcare benefits; the Superintendent or her designee would sign. Item 6.B, the Policyholder Resolution, cites MCL 388.1622f(1) and the June 1, 2012 deadline, notes coverage through MESSA and, as of January 1, 2012, Blue Cross Blue Shield, ADN, National Vision Administrators and Reliance Standard, and resolves that Troy School District is the policyholder of all such policies including all MESSA branded plans.

**Full-Day Kindergarten (report).** Memorandum dated December 1, 2011 from Jan Keeling to Dr. Barbara Fowler, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction, 4400 Livernois, 248/823-4000, fax 248/823-4013, responding to pending legislation changing state funding of kindergarten students and considering full-day kindergarten for 2012-2013; an October report covered an Oakland County district survey, research, a cost comparison against potentially losing half of the foundation allowance per kindergartner, demographics and the Common Core. Dr. Joan Lessen-Firestone, Director of Early Childhood at Oakland Schools, presented "Full-Day Kindergarten: Why Does it Matter?" citing studies of which only one was experimental, four closely matched, two used large databases and control, and seven were fairly recent, and reporting gains in academic achievement, literacy and language (especially for ELL students, lasting through at least middle school), social-emotional conduct, and individualization, with Common Core to be fully implemented in most states by 2014-2015. The preliminary draft timeline runs January 3–31, 2012 (communications pieces), January 3–13 (district kindergarten committee), February 1 (Schools of Choice advertising), February 15 (parent presentation by Joan Firestone), February 22 (Round-Up mailings), March 15 (Somerset kindergartners assigned to Bemis, Morse or Schroeder), March 21–29 (Round-Ups), April 10 (Schools of Choice lottery), April 16–20 (enrollment projections and program relocation), April 20–27 (posting new teaching positions), April 23–27 (SOC building assignments), April 27–May 1 (notification letters), May 7–18 (SOC registration), May 21–June 1 (curriculum and furniture orders) and August 2012 (in-service).

**Summer Success Academy (report).** Presented by Dr. Richard Machesky, Assistant Superintendent for Secondary Instruction. The first program of its kind in the district served 49 students entering 9th grade in 2011-2012 from Baker, Boulan Park, Larson and Smith middle schools moving to Athens and Troy High Schools; 81 students were invited and 53 signed commitment forms. It ran 24 sessions, seven more than normal summer school, from 8:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. with two 90-minute blocks of English and Algebra 1 and one 50-minute study skills class, transportation, light breakfast and lunch, four extended learning opportunities and up to 1.0 elective credit; it was held at NCHS with instructors Anne Costello and Drew LaTorre. Readiness benchmarks cited were ACT Reading 21 and ACT Math 22. First-quarter report cards showed Athens with 26 participants at an average SSA GPA of 2.20 against 1.91 for non-SSA students and average E's of 1.18 against 1.67; Troy had 23 participants at 2.57 against 2.53. Planning has begun for Summer Success Academy 2012.

**Best Practices Incentive.** Section 22f of the State School Aid Act provides $100 per pupil one-time grants to districts satisfying at least four of five criteria not later than June 1, 2012 (MCL 388.1622f). The district certifies it is the designated policyholder for medical benefit plans (22f(1)(b)); will continue implementing a Service Consolidation Plan (22f(1)(c)), a signed board resolution having been sent to the Michigan Department of Education on September 13, 2011 with annual status reports due by February 1; has obtained competitive bids on non-instructional services (22f(1)(d)); and will link the MI School Data Portal dashboard indicators from the district home page (22f(1)(e)). The resolution is to be filed with the State Aid and School Finance Office, with a roll call listing Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Malven, Miletti and Philippart.

**Facilities Study Update.** Co-chairs Greg Bryen and Waqar Hashim presented for the 18-member Facilities Study Team, with recommendations due at the February 7, 2012 meeting. Charges include maximizing use of facilities, ensuring equity among schools, maintaining current grade configurations (K-5, 6-8, 9-12) and the IB K-12 program, excluding vacant properties being monitored for sale, and excluding staffing, program assignment and class size. Step 1 (organize, October) is complete; Step 2 (information gathering, November) is in process with elementary building tours and two task teams; Step 3 (develop recommendation, December) is next.

**Other business.** Citing Board Policy B-2001, Workshops and Conferences, which requires prior approval by resolution for out-of-state meetings, the Board considers Board President Philippart attending the National School Boards Association Annual Federal Relations Network Conference in Washington, D.C., February 5–7, 2012; Troy Schools was one of six districts selected by the Oakland County School Board Association for a $500 scholarship. The final item is a closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), with a roll call of Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Malven, Miletti, Philippart and Underwood.
